findings.title: Use readonly modifier consistently for input type fields
findings.body: The new fields `passed`, `failed`, and `skipped` are marked as `readonly`, but the existing field `passed` in the same type was not. This introduces inconsistent immutability within the same type definition. Apply `readonly` to all fields or none to maintain uniformity.
findings.suggestion:
readonly passed: number
  readonly failed: number
  readonly skipped: number

findings.title: Add readonly modifier to function parameter destructuring
findings.body: The function `formatCheckSummary` destructures its parameter, but the destructured fields are not marked as `readonly`. This could allow accidental reassignment of the input fields within the function. Add `readonly` to the destructured fields to enforce immutability.
findings.suggestion: export function formatCheckSummary({ readonly passed, readonly failed, readonly skipped }: CheckSummaryInput) {

summary.problem: Inconsistent use of the `readonly` modifier in the `CheckSummaryInput` type and its usage in `formatCheckSummary` reduces code clarity and safety.
summary.done_well: The change introduces immutability for the new fields, aligning with modern TypeScript best practices.
